title: 21 Grams
fabula: Mathematician Paul Rivers is told that his failing heart will kill him within weeks unless a donor is found. | His estranged wife Mary presses him to agree to be inseminated with his frozen sperm before he dies. | Ex-convict Jack Jordan, newly born again, holds down a job and coaches boys' baseball while his wife Marianne dreads his fanaticism and his temper. | Cristina Peck, a recovered addict, lives a settled suburban life with her husband Michael and their two young daughters. | Jack's pickup hits Michael and both girls at a crossing; he drives off, turns back, and then flees. | Cristina is told at the hospital that her husband and both children are dead. | Michael's heart is transplanted into Paul, who wakes up alive for the first time in months. | Jack walks into a police station, confesses to the hit-and-run and is sent back to prison. | Cristina goes back to cocaine and begins methodically destroying herself. | Unable to stop thinking about whose heart is beating in his chest, Paul hires a private investigator to find the donor's widow. | Paul follows Cristina, engineers a meeting at a swimming pool, and the two begin an affair. | Paul leaves Mary and tells her he does not want the child she is trying to conceive. | Paul admits to Cristina that he is carrying Michael's heart; she throws him out, then takes him back. | Released early, Jack walks out on Marianne and on his faith and takes work at a motel far from home. | Cristina demands that Jack be killed, and Paul buys a gun and tracks him to the motel. | Paul cannot go through with it and only wounds Jack, telling him to run. | Jack follows the pair back to their motel and asks Paul to finish the job, and Paul turns the gun on himself instead. | Cristina and Jack get the dying Paul to a hospital where the transplanted heart fails; Jack goes home to his family and Cristina, pregnant, goes home alone.

title: Babel

title: The Usual Suspects
fabula: Years earlier in Turkey, Hungarian gangsters hold Keyser Soze's family hostage, and he kills his own wife and children and then everyone connected to the men, and disappears into legend. | Five criminals - Keaton, McManus, Fenster, Hockney and Verbal Kint - are pulled into a truck-hijacking lineup in New York and held overnight in the same cell. | In the cell they plan revenge on the NYPD's "taxi service", a ring of corrupt officers escorting smugglers through the city. | The crew ambush the taxi service, and the ensuing scandal tears the department apart. | Keaton's lawyer and lover Edie Finneran gets them to Los Angeles, where McManus's contact Redfoot buys the stolen jewels. | Redfoot puts them on to a jeweller who turns out to be a Hungarian carrying heroin, and the crew realise they are being steered. | The lawyer Kobayashi appears, says he acts for Keyser Soze, tells each man he has unknowingly stolen from Soze, and orders them to destroy a boatload of his rivals' cocaine. | Fenster runs and is found shot dead on a beach. | The crew try to kill Kobayashi in his office and back off when he reveals he is holding Edie Finneran. | On the night of the raid the four survivors board the Hungarian boat in San Pedro harbour. | Hockney and McManus are killed below decks, and there is no cocaine anywhere on the ship. | Keaton is shot by a figure on deck while Verbal watches from the dockside, and the boat goes up in flames. | Customs agent Dave Kujan interrogates Verbal in a borrowed police office in San Pedro, pressing him to give up Keaton. | A burned Hungarian survivor tells the FBI from his hospital bed that Keyser Soze was on the boat, and begins describing him to a sketch artist. | Verbal, granted immunity, tells Kujan that Keaton was Soze all along, collects his belongings and walks out of the station. | Kujan realises that Verbal improvised the entire story from the noticeboard behind the desk and the maker's name on the bottom of a coffee cup. | Verbal's limp and his crippled hand straighten out as he walks down the street, and Kobayashi collects him in a waiting car. | The faxed sketch finishes printing, and the face on it is Verbal Kint's.

title: Irreversible
fabula: Alex lies in bed with Marcus describing a recurring dream of a red tunnel while the two tease each other about her ex-boyfriend Pierre. | Alone in the flat, Alex takes a pregnancy test and finds that it is positive. | Alex reads in a park among sprinklers and playing children, one hand resting on her stomach. | Alex, Marcus and Pierre ride the Metro to a party, arguing cheerfully about sex and about Marcus's drinking. | At the party Marcus gets steadily drunk and high and starts pursuing other women, and a disgusted Alex leaves on her own. | Rather than cross a busy road Alex takes a pedestrian underpass and walks in on the pimp Le Tenia beating a transsexual woman. | Le Tenia rapes Alex and beats her head against the concrete while a passer-by glimpses them and backs away. | Marcus and Pierre come out of the party to find Alex being loaded into an ambulance. | Two men in the street offer to sell Marcus the rapist's name and steer him and Pierre towards a club called the Rectum. | Marcus hunts through the club, seizes the wrong man and has his arm snapped. | Pierre beats that man's face in with a fire extinguisher while the real Le Tenia watches from a few feet away. | Police handcuff Marcus and Pierre and carry the pair out of the club into the street. | In a flat above that street, an old man tells a younger one that time destroys everything.

title: Vantage Point

fabula: On a hot day in 1935, thirteen-year-old Briony Tallis finishes a play to be performed for her brother's homecoming. | Briony watches from an upstairs window as her sister Cecilia strips to her underwear and climbs into the fountain in front of Robbie Turner, the housekeeper's son. | Robbie drafts a letter of apology to Cecilia, sends the obscene version by mistake, and Briony reads it on the way. | Briony walks in on Robbie and Cecilia making love in the library and takes it for an assault. | The twins run off, and during the search Briony sees Lola being raped in the dark and names Robbie as the man. | Robbie is arrested and taken away in front of the family, and Cecilia breaks with all of them. | In 1940 Robbie is released from prison into the army and is separated from his unit in the retreat across France. | Cecilia, now a nurse in London, writes to Robbie, and the two spend a few hours together on his leave. | Robbie walks to Dunkirk with two corporals and reaches a beach of burning vehicles, shot horses and thousands of waiting men. | Robbie lies down in a cinema on the seafront and dies of septicaemia the night before the evacuation. | Briony, eighteen, takes a nursing place in London instead of Cambridge and treats men brought back from France. | Briony learns that Lola is marrying Paul Marshall, the man who actually raped her. | Briony goes to Cecilia's flat, finds Robbie there, and promises to recant her statement and set the truth down in writing. | Cecilia is killed when a bomb bursts the water main above Balham Underground station in October 1940. | In 1999 the elderly Briony, dying and giving her last interview, admits that she never went to the flat and that Robbie and Cecilia never saw each other again. | Briony says she gave the two of them in her novel the life they were never allowed, and the film shows them together at the seaside cottage.

title: Everything Everywhere All at Once

title: Arcadia

title: Michael Clayton

title: Twelve Monkeys
fabula: A virus released in the mid-nineteen-nineties kills most of the human race and drives the survivors underground. | Decades later the scientists running the underground colony send convicts up to collect specimens, and James Cole volunteers. | Cole is sent back in time, arrives six years too early, and is arrested raving about a plague. | In the asylum the psychiatrist Kathryn Railly interviews Cole, and he meets Jeffrey Goines, the son of a famous virologist. | Cole is pulled back to the future and interrogated about a voicemail recording the scientists have recovered. | Cole is sent to the right year and abducts Railly, who has since written a book about apocalyptic prophecy. | Cole and Railly find graffiti for the Army of the Twelve Monkeys and trace Goines to his father's estate. | Goines denies everything and says the idea of stealing the virus was Cole's own, from the asylum. | Railly comes across a photograph from the First World War of a soldier who is unmistakably Cole. | Cole decides he has been insane all along and asks to be allowed to stay where he is. | Railly finds a bullet fired in 1917 in an X-ray of Cole and understands that he has been telling the truth. | The Army of the Twelve Monkeys turn out to be animal rights activists who release the zoo animals and shut Goines's father in a cupboard. | Cole and Railly go to the airport in disguise to stop the virologist's assistant, who is the real carrier. | Railly spots the carrier, Cole runs at him with a gun, and airport police shoot Cole dead while a small boy watches from the concourse. | The carrier boards his flight with the virus, seated beside one of the scientists from the future.

title: Nashville
fabula: A sound truck for the presidential candidate Hal Phillip Walker circles the city broadcasting his platform to nobody in particular. | The country star Haven Hamilton records a bicentennial anthem while a reporter called Opal wanders the studio talking into a tape recorder. | Barbara Jean, the most loved singer in the city, collapses at her own airport welcome and is taken to hospital. | A pile-up on the freeway strands most of the city's musicians and hangers-on together for an entire afternoon. | Linnea Reese sings with a gospel choir while her husband Del negotiates with the candidate's organiser John Triplette. | The folk trio Tom, Bill and Mary record together while Tom sleeps with women from every other storyline. | Kenny Fraiser arrives in the city carrying a violin case and takes a room from an old man whose wife is dying in hospital. | Winifred, a waitress who has walked out on her husband, keeps trying to get onto any stage that will let her sing. | Sueleen Gay, who cannot sing at all, performs at a men's smoker and is made to strip for the room. | Barbara Jean is let out of hospital and breaks down on stage, rambling to the audience until she is led off. | Haven Hamilton refuses to appear at the candidate's rally unless his own conditions are met. | Linnea sleeps with Tom after his set and goes home afterwards to her deaf children. | The old man's wife dies in hospital, and his lodger does not notice. | Triplette assembles the rally by promising every performer a different thing. | Barbara Jean sings at the rally and is shot in front of the crowd by the young man with the violin case. | Haven Hamilton, hit in the arm, tells the crowd that this is their city and hands the microphone to Winifred. | Winifred takes the stage at last and leads the crowd in a song while the ambulances pull away. | The crowd keeps singing as the camera withdraws over their heads.

title: Grand Hotel

title: Slaughterhouse-Five
fabula: Billy Pilgrim is born in Ilium and grows into a weak, peculiar child. | Billy's father throws him into the deep end of a swimming pool to teach him to swim, and Billy sinks to the bottom. | Billy is drafted as a chaplain's assistant and sent to Europe with no training worth the name. | Billy is lost behind the lines with a scout called Roland Weary, who beats him for wanting to be left to die. | The two are captured, and Weary dies of gangrene on the prison train, blaming Billy with his last breath. | Billy is held in a camp with British officers who have been receiving double rations for years through a clerical error. | Billy is sent on to Dresden and housed with other prisoners in a disused abattoir. | Dresden is destroyed by fire in a single night, and the prisoners in the meat locker come up to find the city gone. | Billy and the others are made to dig bodies out of the cellars until one of the diggers dies of the dry heaves. | Paul Lazzaro, a fellow prisoner, promises to have Billy killed one day on Weary's account. | Billy comes home, collapses, and is hospitalised, where a patient introduces him to the novels of Kilgore Trout. | Billy marries Valencia, the daughter of the optometry school's owner, and becomes a rich man. | Billy survives an air crash in Vermont, and Valencia dies of carbon monoxide poisoning driving to the hospital. | Billy is taken by Tralfamadorians and kept in a zoo on their planet with the film star Montana Wildhack. | The Tralfamadorians explain that all moments exist at once and that free will is an idea peculiar to Earth. | Billy goes on a radio talk show and tries to tell the world about the aliens and the fourth dimension. | Billy's daughter Barbara decides he is senile and takes over his affairs. | Billy is shot dead by a laser gun after addressing a crowd, exactly as he has always known he would be.

title: Catch-22
fabula: Yossarian arrives on the island and flies his first missions as a bombardier. | Snowden is hit over Avignon and dies in Yossarian's arms as Yossarian finds the second wound under his flak suit. | Colonel Cathcart raises the number of missions needed to go home, and then raises it again, and again. | Yossarian reports sick with a liver complaint just short of jaundice and stays in hospital as long as the doctors will allow. | Yossarian censors the enlisted men's letters out of boredom and signs them with a borrowed name. | An investigator arrives to look into the forged signatures and finds nothing at all. | Doc Daneeka explains that asking to be grounded for madness is proof of sanity, and therefore no grounds for anything. | Milo Minderbinder builds a syndicate trading across both sides of the front and corners the entire Egyptian cotton crop. | Milo contracts with the enemy to bomb his own squadron for an agreed fee. | A relentlessly cheerful patient drives every other man out of the ward. | Clevinger is tried for an offence nobody can name, and later flies into a cloud and is never seen again. | Doc Daneeka is recorded as dead because his name was on a flight manifest, and no amount of paperwork can bring him back. | Nately falls in love with a prostitute who is asleep every time he calls. | Nately is killed over Spezia, and his prostitute blames Yossarian and tries to knife him wherever he goes. | The military police turn the apartments out, and Yossarian walks back through the city alone past one atrocity after another. | Aarfy rapes and kills a maid and is not arrested, while Yossarian is arrested for being in the city without a pass. | Cathcart and Korn offer Yossarian a bargain: say the squadron is wonderful and go home a hero. | Yossarian refuses the bargain, learns that Orr has rowed all the way to Sweden, and sets off to follow him.

title: The Limey
fabula: Wilson, a career thief, spends nine years in an English prison while his daughter Jenny grows up without him. | Jenny goes to Los Angeles and takes up with the record producer Terry Valentine. | Jenny works out that Valentine is laundering drug money and threatens to go to the police. | Valentine's head of security kills Jenny and stages a car crash on a canyon road. | Wilson is released, reads a newspaper cutting somebody has posted to him, and flies out. | Wilson finds Ed Roel, an acquaintance of Jenny's, who tells him what little he knows. | Wilson goes to a warehouse to ask questions, is beaten and thrown into the street, and walks back in and kills everyone in it. | Wilson meets Elaine, Jenny's acting teacher, who tells him exactly what sort of father he was. | Wilson and Roel watch Valentine's house from the hills above it. | Wilson crashes a party at the house, and the security men drive him into the desert to shoot him. | Wilson kills the men in the desert and walks back out to the road. | Valentine runs to a beach house up the coast with his young girlfriend. | Wilson and Roel drive north, and Roel is shot dead in the assault on the beach house. | Wilson corners Valentine on the rocks, and Valentine admits the girl's death came out of his own panic. | Wilson lets Valentine live, flies home, and thinks about a day at the seaside with Jenny as a small child.

title: Mirror
fabula: A stammering boy is treated by a hypnotist on television and speaks a clear sentence for the first time. | In the nineteen-thirties Maria sits on a fence outside a country house waiting for a husband who does not come. | A doctor passing on the road stops to talk to Maria, and the fence gives way beneath them both. | A barn burns down at dusk while the family stand in the doorway and watch without moving. | Maria runs through the rain to the printing house certain she has passed a fatal misprint, and finds that she has not. | Alexei's father comes home on leave during the war, and the children are shy with him. | Maria takes Alexei to sell her earrings to a doctor's wife in a warm house, and cannot make herself go through with it. | At a military training camp a boy who has lost his whole family refuses an order and lies down on a grenade. | Alexei's small son Ignat, left alone in the flat, reads a letter aloud to a woman who is not there. | In the present Alexei quarrels with his former wife Natalia down the telephone about their son. | Alexei watches his mother, old now, walk across a field with two children. | Alexei lies ill in a darkened room while the doctors agree there is nothing physically wrong with him. | Alexei remembers a girl at school with a cracked lip whom he could never bring himself to speak to. | A gust of wind crosses a field of buckwheat towards the house, and nobody in the house remarks on it. | An old woman leads two children across a meadow at dusk while the camera withdraws into the trees.

syuzhet_notes: The film moves between three periods without a single caption, using the same actress for the mother and the wife and the same boy for the son and the father's son, so even the period of a shot is often undecidable at the time.
fabula_notes: The chronology given here is the most defensible reading: the childhood scenes precede the war, which precedes the narrator's illness. The film itself never commits to it, and other orderings of the childhood material are arguable.

title: The Tree of Life
fabula: Mrs O'Brien is taught by nuns that there are two ways through life, the way of nature and the way of grace. | Mr and Mrs O'Brien marry and their first son Jack is born. | Two more sons follow, and the three boys run wild through the summers of a small Texas town. | Mr O'Brien drills the boys in discipline at the dinner table and teaches the middle one the guitar. | Mrs O'Brien plays with the boys on the lawn while their father is away on business. | Jack, jealous and confused, breaks a neighbour's window and steals a slip from a woman's drawer. | Jack takes his brother into the yard and persuades him to put a finger over an air rifle, then shoots him. | Mr O'Brien loses his job when the plant closes and the family have to leave the house. | Jack asks his brother's forgiveness in a doorway without being able to say any of the words. | A telegram arrives to say the middle brother has died at nineteen, and Mrs O'Brien cannot be consoled. | Mr O'Brien tells Jack that he was too hard on all of them. | The universe forms, stars collapse, the earth cools, and the first life appears in the sea. | A wounded creature lies in a river bed while another puts a foot on its head and then lets it live. | Jack, a middle-aged architect in a glass tower, cannot get through the anniversary of his brother's death. | Jack walks through a doorway standing alone in a desert and finds everyone he has lost gathered on a shore.

title: Waltz with Bashir
fabula: As a young conscript, Ari lands on the coast with an armoured column. | Ari's unit fires all night at a car approaching a roadblock and finds a family inside it in the morning. | A soldier called Carmi swims out to sea from a burning landing craft and survives when the rest of his unit does not. | A soldier named Frenkel dances with a machine gun down a boulevard under sniper fire, beneath posters of the assassinated president-elect. | Ari's unit shells an orchard and a boy with a rocket launcher is killed in front of them. | Ari and two others bathe in the sea at night under flares while the city burns behind them. | Militia enter the refugee camps while the army lights the sky above them. | Over two days the militia kill the people in the camps, while the soldiers on the rooftops fail to understand what they are watching. | Ari stands at the edge of the camp as the women come out screaming. | Twenty-four years later a friend tells Ari over a drink about a recurring dream of twenty-six dogs. | Ari realises he remembers nothing at all of the war and goes looking for the men he served with. | A psychologist explains to Ari that memory can be built out of what a person needs rather than what happened. | A television reporter tells Ari what he saw in the camps and what he said to the defence minister on the telephone. | Ari understands that the flare-lit memory of himself in the sea is a screen he built to stand between himself and the camps.

title: Beloved
fabula: Sethe is brought as a girl to a Kentucky farm and chooses Halle from among the men there. | Baby Suggs is bought out of slavery by Halle's extra labour and settles in a house outside Cincinnati. | A new owner the slaves call schoolteacher arrives at the farm and begins measuring them and writing them up in a book. | Sethe overhears schoolteacher telling his nephews to list her animal characteristics on one side of the page and her human ones on the other. | The men at the farm lay a plan to run, and the plan collapses. | Schoolteacher's nephews hold Sethe down in the barn and take her milk while Halle watches from the loft and loses his mind. | Sethe, pregnant and beaten, walks north alone, and a white girl called Amy Denver delivers her baby in a boat. | Sethe reaches the house and has twenty-eight days of freedom, and Baby Suggs holds a feast for ninety people. | Schoolteacher comes to the house to take Sethe and the children back. | Sethe carries the children into the woodshed and cuts her elder daughter's throat with a handsaw. | Sethe is jailed and released, Baby Suggs takes to her bed and dies, and the neighbours stop coming to the house. | Sethe's two sons run away from a house haunted by the dead baby. | Paul D, one of the men from the farm, arrives after eighteen years and drives the ghost out of the house. | A young woman calling herself Beloved walks out of the water and comes to live with them. | Paul D is moved out of the house room by room and is finally taken to bed by Beloved in the shed. | Stamp Paid shows Paul D the newspaper cutting about the killing, and Paul D leaves. | Beloved swells and consumes Sethe, until thirty women come into the yard and sing until she is gone.

title: The Burning Plain
fabula: In a border town, Gina, a married mother of four, meets a farmer named Nick and the two begin an affair in a trailer out in the fields. | Gina's daughter Mariana discovers the affair and follows her mother out to the trailer. | A gas leak sets the trailer alight and both Gina and Nick are killed in it. | Mariana is left to raise her younger sisters while her father drinks and blames himself. | Nick's son Santiago comes to the town to look at the wreck and to find out who the woman was. | Mariana and Santiago recognise each other and, out of grief more than anything, become lovers. | Mariana burns down her own family's house with her father's photographs inside it. | Mariana finds she is pregnant, and the two of them run away together. | Santiago is badly hurt when their car leaves the road, and Mariana is told he is dead. | Mariana gives birth to a daughter, leaves her with Santiago's family, and disappears. | Living under the name Sylvia, Mariana runs a restaurant on the northern coast, sleeps with men she does not know, and cuts herself. | Santiago, alive and badly scarred, works as a crop duster with his young daughter Maria beside him. | Santiago crashes his aircraft, and Maria is brought north by his friend Carlos to look for her mother. | Carlos finds Sylvia and tells her that Santiago is alive and that her daughter is with him. | Sylvia flies south, and mother and daughter meet each other in a hospital corridor.

title: Je t'aime, je t'aime
fabula: Claude Ridder meets Catrine at a party and the two begin living together. | Catrine is cold and low all the time, and keeps the heating up in a flat Claude finds airless. | Claude and Catrine take a holiday in Scotland, where she is happier for a fortnight. | Claude has an affair with a colleague and says nothing about it to Catrine. | Catrine dies of gas in the flat while Claude is out walking. | The police question Claude, decide it was an accident, and he says nothing about the tap. | Claude tries to shoot himself and only wounds himself. | Claude spends a year in hospital and comes out with nothing to do and nobody expecting him. | Two researchers approach Claude at the hospital gates and ask him to be their first human subject, on the grounds that a man who does not care whether he lives is exactly what they need. | Claude is driven to a laboratory in the country and shown a machine shaped like an enormous soft brain. | Claude is sealed inside with a mouse and sent back exactly one year for exactly one minute, to swim in the sea. | The machine misfires, and Claude begins reliving fragments of his life in no order at all, the same seconds over and over. | The researchers lose control of the machine, cannot bring Claude back, and search the grounds for him. | Claude is found on the lawn outside the laboratory, shot through the chest by his own hand, and dies.
